Novak Djokovic. A Serbian tennis champion who won twenty-four Grand Slam singles titles, surpassing Rafael Nadal as the player with the most major championships in history. His exceptional defensive abilities, mental toughness, and consistency from 2011 onward made him the defining player of the 2010s and early 2020s. He won ten Australian Opens, seven Wimbledons, four US Opens, and three French Opens across his career. He achieved the Calendar Year Golden Slam in 2016, winning all four majors plus Olympic gold in a single year, one of only two men to accomplish this remarkable feat. Known for his extraordinary defense, flexibility, and remarkable ability to hit groundstrokes from seemingly impossible positions, his return of serve is considered among the best ever. He reached world number one in 2011 and held the ranking for over 370 weeks, with his dominance particularly strong from 2011 to 2015 and 2018 to 2023, rivaling the eras of Federer and Nadal. He is a member of the "Big Three" with Federer and Nadal; their rivalry shaped tennis's competitive landscape over two decades. He made controversial pandemic-related decisions including vaccine hesitancy and missing tournaments that affected his legacy and record, though his on-court achievements remain extraordinary and unmatched in terms of his consistency.
